local.title: Overgrown shrubs and **sunken borders.**
local.intro: Most homes in Flint were built before 1960, and their foundation beds have usually been replanted a few times since. What is left is often a mix: shrubs that cover the windows, a border sunk into the lawn, and soil that has been dug and filled more than once.

points.title: Shrubs that outgrew the house
points.body: Foundation shrubs planted decades ago can cover a porch rail and half a window. We take them out with a compact track loader, roots and all, so the new bed starts clean.

points.title: Ground that has been moved before
points.body: In parts of Flint the soil has been cut, moved or filled over the years. A bed dug in that ground can turn up almost anything, so Rob plans for the haul off up front.

points.title: Heavy, slow draining soil
points.body: Much of the city sits on soil that drains slowly. Beds get shaped so water runs away from the foundation, and plants get picked for ground that stays damp into spring.

points.title: The strip by the street is the city's
points.body: Work in the public right of way, including digging, takes a city permit, and street trees there are the city's to assess. New beds stay on your side of the walk unless the city has signed off.

logistics.title: How a Flint landscaping job comes together.
body: Rob comes out, looks at the house and the beds with you, suggests what to keep and what to pull, and quotes a price for the whole job. You know what is happening and what it costs before anything gets dug.

On the work days, the track loader digs out old shrubs and borders, the crew sets the new block wall or cuts the natural edge, lays fabric, plants, and finishes with black, brown or red mulch. Old plants, borders and soil leave in our trailer, not in your yard waste bags.
Big trees are a job for a tree company, and street trees are the city's. Bushes and small trees inside your beds, we can take out.

faq.q: Is there a landscaper who works in Flint, MI?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes does landscaping in Flint: overgrown shrubs and old borders out, block walls or a natural edge in, then new plants, fabric and mulch. We are based in Grand Blanc, licensed and insured, and the estimate is free.

faq.q: Can you take out the old bushes in front of my house?
faq.a: Yes. We dig out overgrown bushes and small trees with a compact track loader, roots and all, then rebuild the bed. Big trees go to a tree company. See [bush and small tree removal](/bush-removal/) for how that part works.

faq.q: Do I need a permit to dig a bed between the sidewalk and the street in Flint?
faq.a: Usually, yes. The city says work in the public right of way, including excavating, needs a permit from Building and Safety Inspections at City Hall, and street trees there are the city's to assess. Check with the city before planning a bed out there.

faq.q: Can you replace an old brick border with something cleaner?
faq.a: Yes. The old brick comes out, a gray block wall or a cut natural edge goes in, and the bed gets fabric and fresh mulch. See [bed edging and block walls](/bed-edging-and-block-walls/).

faq.q: Do you just mulch, without a full redo?
faq.a: Yes. If the plants are fine and the beds only need weeding, a fresh edge and new mulch, that is a smaller job: see [mulch installation in Flint](/mulch-installation-flint-mi/).
